column1: # How long each browser suite takes, so `run.js` can pack them into shards.
# A WEIGHT IS A MEASUREMENT WITH A DATE, NEVER A FACT. These decide which shard a suite lands
# in and nothing else: coverage is proven from the receipts each shard writes, so a stale
# weight costs wall clock and cannot cost correctness. That is the whole reason this file is
# allowed to exist at all — it is the one typed list in this directory, and it is typed
# because a duration cannot be read off disk. Everything a green run DEPENDS on is still
# MEASURED: 31 suites, one serial pass, this machine, 2026-09-10 at 43da6710.
# Every suite exited 0 in that pass. Two consecutive runs of the heavier suites were
# within a second of each other, so these are not single-sample noise.
#   heaviest suite       110 s (splash.js) — the floor: no shard count gets under it
# AND THEY ARE LOCAL SECONDS, WHICH IS THE THING TO KNOW BEFORE TRUSTING THEM. The same tree
# took 1792 s serially on `macos-latest` (run 34435558131) against 756 s here, so the runner
# is roughly 2.4x slower and these numbers are RELATIVE weights that happen to be in seconds.
# Packing only needs the ratios, which is why this is honest input for the first sharded run
# and not the last word: re-derive it from that run's own receipts, which carry each suite's
# wall clock on the runner. Numbers from one execution are comparable with each other and
# numbers stitched from several sources are not.
# A suite missing from this file is NOT an error. `run.js` packs it as the heaviest known
# suite and NAMES it in `--plan`, so it lands in the emptiest shard and somebody can see that
# its weight was assumed. Adding a suite therefore needs no edit here.
# Longest first, which is also the order the packer walks them in.
